label: mapped-host all-layer gather for small bulk inputs
hypothesis: For 8..16-token bulk inputs, gather all layers directly from the pinned CPU table using GPU IDs in one kernel, avoiding CPU ID staging, gather and separate H2D.
expected_bottleneck: Mapped-bulk diagnostic b8 0.061450 to 0.033291 ms; b16 0.105814 to 0.048239 ms. b1 is slightly slower, so exclude it before model timing.
change: Mapped bulk only for existing bulk policy and 8..16 tokens. Pin CPU table during setup; preserve ordinary pipeline and other bulk lookup algorithms. Fresh IDs and CPU table values on every call. Final read-stream synchronization preserves host mutation/lifetime safety.
tradeoffs: 3000 MiB folded CPU table becomes pinned; count it once alongside every cached host buffer.
Mapped reads use GPU resources; microbench improvement may not translate to model latency.
Primary target is b8 decode only; b1/decode and prefill algorithm fluctuations cannot qualify as the proposed gain.

decision: All twelve screen jobs completed. Target b8 decode slower 0.025238 ms versus A0001 and absolute gap worse 0.006473 ms. No target benefit; reject without confirmation/full/generation. b16 decode descriptive improvement is secondary and cannot substitute for the fixed primary target. Prefill and b1 algorithms do not establish a mapped-bulk gain.
next_insight: Tiny mapped-bulk component savings do not establish whole-model improvement; GPU launch/dependency and host-lifetime costs were not causally isolated. Restore ordinary CPU table and A0001 transport.
